WE PROUDLY PRACTICE
Organic Regenerative Farming

We know that the quality of our cheeses and yogurts is intimately tied to the health of our land and animals. Since we started farming this land in 1959 we've practiced regenerative farming - though we didn't label it regenerative back then; it was just farming. In a nutshell (in a cheese rind?), this means meeting all the organic standards required to be certified organic while also increasing the ecological diversity of our soils. 

The cows graze on pasture, we use the cow's manure to fertilize the land, and then we hay our fields to feed our herd throughout the winter. The cow's milk is turned into cheese and the by-product of cheesemaking, whey, is fed to our forest-raised pigs. The cheeses, yogurts, and meats feed us and our community, and our community supports our family run farm with every purchase.

Local, affordable, pasture raised meat

Here at von Trapp Farmstead we believe that fostering a relationship between the consumer and the farmer is the best way to re-localize our food system. Our regeneratively raised pork & beef products are available exclusively through our Farm Store, while our salami is available seasonally in our online store. 

Whey Fed Pork

Our pastured, whey-fed pigs are a vital part of our regenerative farming practices, helping enrich our fields for future grazing and consuming products that would otherwise go to waste. Along with the organic whey from our cheese production, they eat spent brewing grains from Lawson’s Finest Liquids, leftover breads from Red Hen Bakery, and various vegetable and grain byproducts from local food production.

Their diet produces distinctive, flavorsome meat with rich fat and savory maple notes. Our store is stocked with ground pork, linked sausages, bacon, roasts, and other cuts of meat.

Beef

Our herd of cows is raised on the farm's organic pasture with minimal supplemental grain. By the end of their milking careers, years of grazing has given our beef a full-bodied, mature flavor with superior marbling. Our herd includes genetics from a range of heritage dual-purpose breeds including Jersey, Ayrshire, Montbeliarde, and Normande. We are always stocked with ground beef, beef for stew, tenderloin and minute steaks.

Please note, while our animals are certified organic, our processing partner is not, so our beef is not certified organic.

A Selection of Salamis

Our whey-fed pork salami is sold exclusively through our farm store and in a selection of our curated gift boxes. 

SAUCISSON SEC 

This classic French style of salami has classic black pepper and garlic seasonings offering rich, complex, meaty flavors with a pleasant fruity funk and clean pepper bite. It pairs beautifully with farmhouse ales, lush IPAs, or flavorful wines. Enjoy with fresh bread, honey or apricot mustard, and, of course, any of our farmstead cheeses! 

SOPPRESSATA

This salami features classic black pepper and garlic accompanied by red pepper flakes to give a hint of spice that won't make you sweat but brings the aromatic peppery flavors to the top of your tongue.  This salami pairs well with IPA’s, aromatic whites and, of course, von Trapp farmstead cheeses! 

FINOCCHIONA 

Finocchiona is a balanced salami with toasted fennel seeds and roasted garlic.  The herbs and whey-fed pork meld together in beautiful harmony.  Pairs well with bloomy rind cheeses, dried fruit and light ales and wines alike.

HOW TO GET HERE

Coming from the North:

Take Route 100 south towards Waitsfield. Before you enter town proper, turn left onto Tremblay Road. At the T, turn right and go up North Road. As you approach the top, you’ll see the cemetery on your right - take a left onto Common Road (a dirt road). You’ll drive through a beautiful tunnel of big maple trees, pass the von Trapp Greenhouses on the right, and then will see our Farm Store sign on the left! Park in the lot, say hi to the chickens, and come on in!

Coming from the South:

Take Route 100 north to Waitsfield, and turn right on Bridge Street. At the Y, veer left up Joslin Hill Road. When you get to the top of the hill, turn right onto Common Road (a dirt road) across from the cemetery. You’ll drive through a beautiful tunnel of big maple trees, pass the von Trapp Greenhouses on the right, and then will see our Farm Store sign on the left! Park in the lot, say hi to the chickens, and come on in!

Organic Raw Milk CSA

Just like a vegetable CSA, with our milk CSA you pay upfront for a full season of weekly organic raw milk. A season for our raw milk CSA is 13 weeks. 

One share is one (1) half gallon of milk every week for 13 weeks. Sign up for 2 shares if you want a full gallon (2 jars) every week. We will prorate the cost if you’d like to join mid-season. The cost of each 13-week share is $78, plus a $5/bottle deposit. Two shares (1 gallon) is $156, plus (2) $5/bottle deposits. You can pay with cash or card in our farm store. 

CSA pick up is at our Farm Store.  We ask that you return your clean bottles and lids when you pick up your next CSA share. It is okay to skip a week, but ideally you are bringing in clean, empty bottles each week during pick up.

If you will be out of town, please let us know so we don’t bottle milk for you that week. If you do not let us know you’ll be out of town, you forfeit your milk for that week. 

Click the button below to complete the sign up form, & we’ll get in touch with you to finalize details. You can also email info@vontrappfarmstead.com with questions about the raw milk CSA. 

SIGN UP FOR THE CSA

The State of Vermont requires you read and sign that you understand the risks of drinking raw milk when you come in to pick up your first jar of milk. The statement will read: “Consuming raw or unpasteurized milk may cause illness, particularly in children, seniors, persons with weakened immune systems, and pregnant women.” You may preview the waiver here, or even print it out & bring it in for your first pick up!

The von Trapp Farmstead
THREE GENERATIONS OF SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE

Our family has run the von Trapp Farmstead since 1959, when Werner and Erika von Trapp moved to Waitsfield, Vermont to grow crops and raise livestock, and to build a sustainable future for their children. Today, we make award winning cheese, organic yogurt, and pastured meat from our regeneratively raised cows and pigs. We believe that wholesome, flavorful food begins with healthy soil and animals. Our products are infused with a deep appreciation & desire to honor the land and cows that allow us to practice our craft.

Sebastian von Trapp grew up on the family farm, with his Opa and Oma (Werner and Erika) living just down the road. His parents, Martin and Kelly, ran the farm and dairy, selling their milk to local buyers at whatever price was set by the whims of the global dairy market. In 2007, he began construction on a creamery for making cheese out of the farm’s milk, with the goal of creating more sustainable income for the farm. The von Trapp Farmstead started making cheese in 2009.

Molly Semler grew up in Middlesex, Vermont and returned to the state to follow her passion for making cheese. She started working on the farm over a decade ago, and over the course of making cheese together, she and Sebastian fell in love. (Cheesy, but true!) Sebastian currently runs the farm while Molly operates the creamery. In 2020, we opened a farm store to sell our products directly to locals and visitors.

Each of our cheeses draws on the von Trapp family’s Austrian roots, with distinctive flavors born from traditional cheesemaking techniques. They’re made literally from the ground up, with respect for the soil that grows the grass that feeds our cows. As farmstead cheesemakers, we can look out the window and see the cows that produced the milk we are turning into cheese or yogurt.

We proudly practice regenerative farming methods that go above and beyond organic standards to cultivate a diverse ecosystem on our farm. Come visit our farm store, or try our products online; we think you’ll taste the difference.

von Trapp Family History
View fullsize
View fullsize
View fullsize
View fullsize

The Sound of Music has made "von Trapp" a household name across generations. While aspects of the movie are accurate, many details were changed or dramatized by Hollywood. The family didn't traverse the Alps on foot with all their instruments, but they did leave Austria to avoid the Nazi regime, by taking a train to Italy and touring around Europe and the United States, eventually settling in Stowe in the 1940s.

Werner and Erika von Trapp started the von Trapp Family Farm in Waitsfield, Vermont in 1959. Erika (lovingly called Oma, like the cheese made in her honor) had studied agriculture in Austria and was a main force behind establishing and growing the farm. 

Now over 65 years later, von Trapp Farmstead produces sustainably raised meat and dairy; live-culture yogurt, and award-winning artisan cheese from our organic milk. Until his death in 2023, Martin, one of Werner and Erika's six children, and his wife Kelly operated the organic dairy. Now Martin and Kelly’s eldest son Sebastian and his wife Molly run the farm in addition to the creamery.

Other members of the von Trapp family operate separate businesses in the region. Johannes von Trapp, the youngest child of Georg and Maria, and his descendents operate the Trapp Family Lodge and von Trapp Brewing at the site of the family’s original home in Stowe. Our relatives Tobias (Tobi) and Sally opened the von Trapp Greenhouses just across the road from our farmstead, and now their daughter Emily operates von Trapp Flowers on the same land.

While these businesses act independently, we often collaborate with each other. For example, we sell von Trapp beer and flowers in our farm store, the von Trapp Bierhall uses our cheese in their kitchens, and we regularly work with the brewery to make our seasonal beer-washed cheese, Drunk Alice.
